findings.claim: Atoms are incredibly small — about 0.1 nanometres across.
findings.truth: 0.1 nm is the atomic RADIUS, not the diameter. The spec states 'Atoms are very small, having a radius of about 0.1 nm (1 x 10-10 m).' Stating it as a width doubles the figure a student would use.

findings.claim: if an atom was the size of a football, a football would be the size of Earth!
findings.truth: The analogy is out by about 20x. Scaling an atom of radius 1e-10 m up to a football (radius 0.11 m) is a factor of 1.1e9; the football then becomes 1.2e8 m, about 19 Earth radii. A marble (radius about 6 mm) gives the factor 5.8e7 that turns a football into the Earth (radius 6.37e6 m).
findings.evidence: recomputation: 0.11 / 1e-10 = 1.1e9; 0.11 x 1.1e9 = 1.2e8 m vs Earth radius 6.37e6 m

findings.claim: Question types '9 marks — Evaluate' and '12 marks + 4 SPaG — Extended', with a mark scheme awarding 4 marks for spelling, punctuation, grammar and specialist terminology.
findings.truth: This board's Combined Science papers are 70 marks in 1 hour 15 minutes and carry no SPaG marks at all; the longest item is a 6-mark extended response. A 12+4 mark question would be 23% of one paper. Both questions retyped as 6 marks with rewritten band ladders. Lesson 1 is the only lesson in the unit with these types; every other lesson tops out at 6.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 (Chemistry Paper 1: 1 hour 15 minutes, 70 marks, 16.7%); 'spelling'/'SPaG' appear nowhere in the spec

findings.claim: Who proposed the plum pudding model of the atom in 1897?
findings.truth: Thomson discovered the electron in 1897; he set out the plum pudding model in 1904. The spec requires no dates, so the date is removed rather than corrected.

findings.claim: A 'Transition Metals' section taught alongside Groups 0, 1 and 7 with no scope label.
findings.truth: Trilogy 5.1.2 runs 5.1.2.1 to 5.1.2.6 and stops at Group 7; there is no transition metals statement. The section is labelled as separate Chemistry only rather than deleted. The lesson also keeps a transition-metal flashcard, which Tom may want to drop.
findings.evidence: spec 5.1.2; 'transition metal' returns no match in the whole spec

findings.claim: The elements also have lower melting points and higher densities going down the group.
findings.truth: The melting point trend is right. Group 1 density does not rise monotonically: potassium (0.86 g/cm3) is less dense than sodium (0.97 g/cm3). The density claim is removed; the spec asks students to predict from GIVEN trends, so no trend needs asserting.
findings.evidence: spec 5.1.2.5; settled densities Li 0.53, Na 0.97, K 0.86, Rb 1.53, Cs 1.88 g/cm3

findings.claim: Concentration can be measured in g/dm3 (mass concentration) or mol/dm3 (molar concentration). Both are essential for different types of calculations.
findings.truth: Only g/dm3 is in scope. Spec 5.3.2.5 defines concentration as mass per given volume of solution; the string 'mol/dm' does not appear anywhere in the Trilogy spec, at either tier. The key fact now says which unit Combined Science needs.
findings.evidence: spec 5.3.2.5; grep 'mol/dm' over the spec returns nothing

findings.claim: 'One _____ equals 1000 cm3.' Options: dm3 / m3 / mm3 / litre. Keyed answer: dm3.
findings.truth: Two options were correct: a litre is also 1000 cm3, and the lesson itself states '1 dm3 = 1000 cm3 = 1000 ml = 1 litre'. A student choosing 'litre' was marked wrong for a true answer. Distractor changed to millilitre (1 cm3).
findings.evidence: lesson content n23; settled SI fact

findings.claim: The most reactive metals (potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium) react vigorously with water and acids.
findings.truth: Magnesium reacts with cold water only very slowly, and aluminium appears not to react at all because of its oxide layer. Teaching that they react vigorously with water is the 'all metals react with water' misconception stated as fact. The spec limits these reactions to room temperature and excludes steam.
findings.evidence: spec 5.4.1.2 ('The reactions of metals with water and acids are limited to room temperature and do not include reactions with steam')

findings.claim: The reactivity series (most to least reactive): K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, C, Zn, Fe, H, Cu, Ag, Au.
findings.truth: Lithium is missing. The spec names it in the set of metals students must place in order, between sodium and calcium. The revision tip on this box tells students to write out the full series, so the omission is taught.
findings.evidence: spec 5.4.1.2 ('potassium, sodium, lithium, calcium, magnesium, zinc, iron and copper')

findings.claim: To make a pure, dry salt ... This is Required Practical 1.
findings.truth: In Combined Science the salt preparation is Required practical activity 8. Required practical 1 is the light-microscope biology practical. (It is number 1 only in separate Chemistry.)

findings.claim: Required Practical 4 involves electrolysing aqueous solutions ... (repeated in two flashcards).
findings.truth: Electrolysis of aqueous solutions is Required practical activity 9 in Combined Science. Required practical 4 is the amylase/pH biology practical. Number 4 is not the separate-Chemistry number either (that is 3), so it is simply wrong. Three occurrences corrected.

findings.claim: A whole lesson on transition metals and nanoparticles inside a Combined Science Chemistry Paper 1 unit, with no scope label.
findings.truth: Neither topic is in the Trilogy spec: 'transition metal' and 'nanoparticle' return no match anywhere in it. In separate Chemistry, nanoparticles also sit under Using resources (Chemistry Paper 2), so the lesson is misplaced twice over. Every fact and calculation in it checks out (iron mp 1538 degC, sodium 98 degC; 1 cm cube 6 cm2 cut to 1 mm cubes gives 60 cm2; 2 cm cube ratio 24/8 = 3:1; PM2.5 100-2500 nm; coarse 2500-10000 nm), so the content is kept and labelled rather than deleted. Tom to decide whether to retire it, move it to a separate-Chemistry board, or leave it labelled.
findings.evidence: spec 5.1.2 and 5.10; grep 'transition metal' / 'nanoparticle' over the spec returns nothing

findings.claim: A whole lesson on percentage yield, atom economy, mol/dm3 concentration and molar gas volume inside a Combined Science unit, with mol/dm3 and gas volumes flagged only as Higher tier.
findings.truth: None of the four topics is in the Trilogy spec. Quantitative chemistry (5.3) ends at limiting reactants and concentration in g/dm3; 'percentage yield', 'atom economy', 'mol/dm' and 'molar volume' all return no match. Marking them Higher tier implies Higher students are examined on them, which is wrong. All arithmetic in the lesson is correct (CaCO3 atom economy 56/100 = 56%; 0.5 mol in 0.25 dm3 = 2.0 mol/dm3; 0.3 x 24 = 7.2 dm3; 7.2/8.0 = 90%; 0.50 x 0.025 = 0.0125 mol), so the content is kept and labelled.
findings.evidence: spec 5.3.1-5.3.2.5; grep 'atom economy' / 'percentage yield' / 'mol/dm' / '24 dm' over the spec returns nothing

findings.claim: A whole lesson on titrations, chemical cells and fuel cells inside a Combined Science unit. Only the titration practical carries a 'separate Chemistry' note.
findings.truth: None of the three topics is in the Trilogy spec. Trilogy 5.4.2 has no titration statement and no titration required practical; Trilogy 5.5 ends at 5.5.1.3 (bond energies) with no 5.5.2 on cells. All chemistry in the lesson is correct (0.10 x 0.025 = 0.0025 mol, /0.020 = 0.125 mol/dm3; 0.20 x 0.025 = 0.005 mol, 2:1 gives 0.0025 mol, /0.0125 = 0.20 mol/dm3; H2 -> 2H+ + 2e- and O2 + 4H+ + 4e- -> 2H2O both balance), so the content is kept and labelled.
findings.evidence: spec 5.4.2, 5.5, 10.2; grep 'titration' / 'fuel cell' / 'chemical cell' over the spec returns nothing

findings.claim: Higher-tier-only material is presented to Foundation students across the unit. Lesson 9 is the worst case: the opening key fact ('Energy is required to break chemical bonds and energy is released when new bonds are formed'), the whole 'Bond Breaking and Bond Making' section, knowledge check 4, practice questions 4 and 6 and four flashcards all sit outside any higher-only block. Also: lesson 6 key fact n13 gives the electron definitions of oxidation and reduction; lesson 7 conclusion bullet n21 and knowledge check 4 teach strong and weak acids; lesson 8 paragraph n5 and practice question 2 use electron transfer at the electrodes; lesson 5's practice questions, knowledge checks and flashcards are almost all moles work.
findings.truth: In Trilogy the bond-energy account of exothermic and endothermic reactions is 5.5.1.3 (HT only); the Foundation statement 5.5.1.1 is 'Limited to measurement of temperature change'. Oxidation and reduction in terms of electrons is 5.4.1.4 (HT only), strong and weak acids 5.4.2.5 (HT only), half equations 5.4.3.5 (HT only), moles 5.3.2 (HT only). The lessons already use higher-only divs, so the gap is deliberate-looking but wrong. Two options: (a) wrap the leaked content_html blocks in higher-only, which also needs each affected narration chunk stamped tier:'higher' in the narration manifest or Foundation students will hear text they cannot see (js/main.js filters on manifest entry.tier); or (b) leave content as is and accept that Foundation students over-revise. Recommendation: (a), but it needs a narration re-stamp pass, so it is not a surgical text edit. Practice questions, knowledge checks and flashcards have no tier field at all, so those need a product decision from Tom.
findings.evidence: spec 5.5.1.1, 5.5.1.3, 5.4.1.4, 5.4.2.5, 5.4.3.5, 5.3.2; css/style.css body.tier-foundation .higher-only; js/main.js narration tier filter

summary: Twelve lessons checked against the Combined Science: Trilogy spec. Lessons 10, 11 and 12 are wholly outside the qualification (transition metals, nanoparticles, percentage yield, atom economy, mol/dm3, molar gas volume, titrations, chemical cells, fuel cells return no match in the spec); their chemistry is sound, so each is labelled 'separate Chemistry only' at the top of the content and in the description rather than deleted. Lesson 1 carried invented exam formats (a 9-mark question and a 12-mark + 4 SPaG question; this board's papers are 70 marks with no SPaG). Two required practicals were numbered with the separate-Chemistry or simply wrong index. Every worked example, half equation and answer key in the unit recomputed clean except one knowledge check with two correct options.
